thread:
incidents-bot: ALERT: streaming-p95 has breached SLO in eu-prod for the last 3m. p95=1.20s (SLO=700ms), p99=4.30s. Error rate stable. Affected endpoint: /v1/stream/ (SSE + WS). Detected increase in socket stalls and chunk buffering. paging: yes. Triggered paging and on-call.
Ryan: taking on-call. I see the alert, joining. what's the customer impact? :eyes:
Maya: i'm seeing elevated write buffer sizes on the streaming-proxy (eu) and many connections in CLOSE_WAIT. Looks like proxies are hitting backpressure when clients slow-consume.
Ana: confirmed. From logs: `proxy_write_buf` growth correlates with p99 jumps. Sample log: `streaming-proxy[e0]: write to socket blocked (10s) client=10.10.20.45 route=/v1/stream/` . Also seeing repeated TLS handshake retries for a small subset of clients.
Jay: runtime note: model runtimes are healthy; token generation latency unchanged. This looks networking/proxy-side, not model. We should triage proxy thread pool and TCP settings.
Liz: support: we've got a support case from AcmeCorp (CASE-2026-112). They report stalled streams and hanging responses. They've been rate-limited by their client (long GC pauses) but it results in sockets not reading.
Bob: Acme says impact is partial — about 7% of their streaming sessions stall after 30s. They have long-lived clients, some behind corporate proxies with aggressive windowing.
Ryan: quick mitigation plan ideas: 1) free up proxy workers (scale streaming-proxy), 2) enable aggressive keepalive + shorter socket timeout to free stuck connections, 3) enable fallback to polling for heavy customers temporarily.
Maya: running quick checks: `kubectl --context=prod -n streaming get pods -l app=streaming-proxy -o wide` shows 3 pods, CPU at 60% and net TX spiking. I'm going to scale to 8 to handle connection churn.
Maya: command run: ```
kubectl --context=prod -n streaming scale deployment streaming-proxy --replicas=8
``` 
Maya: scaling started. ETA ~30s for pods warm.
Ana: while that ramps, propose to reduce proxy idle timeout from 120s -> 30s and tcp_keepalive_time from 7200s -> 120s for the proxy pods. That will drop slow clients faster and free buffers.
Jay: quick check: changing keepalive has consequences on some mobile SDKs. We should scope to eu cluster only and add an allowlist for known sensitive customers. I'll prepare a k8s patch for the config map.
Ryan: go for config change. Also enable `envoy.upstream.flush_on_stream_end=true` variant for streaming routes to ensure buffered chunks flush sooner.
Maya: patch applied to configmap: ```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  proxy_idle_timeout: "30s"
  tcp_keepalive_time: "120s"
  envoy_flush_on_stream_end: "true"
``` 
Maya: rolling restart for streaming-proxy triggered.
Ana: logs after first restart: `proxy[e1]: closed idle socket client=10.11.12.13 reason=keepalive-timeout` — good, buffers reclaimed. Early signal: p95 down to ~900ms after scaling + timeout changes.
Ryan: good. Next: enable per-tenant fallback policy in routing: if a client connection stalls >20s, route their sessions to polling (non-streaming) endpoint to avoid blocking resources.
Jay: added canary flag `streaming.fallback.polling.on_stall=true` in routing policy for AcmeCorp and internal test tenants. Deployed canary to 10% traffic. No errors so far.
Liz: notifying Acme support: "We've scaled proxy layer and reduced idle timeouts. We're also enabling a temporary polling fallback for affected sessions. Please try reproducing and tell us if you still see stalls." Sent message, case updated.
Bob: Acme responded: they see immediate improvement for some sessions but still 2-3% stalls. They can tolerate polling fallback for now.
Ana: diagnostic notes: tcpdump on one affected host shows many clients with zero window advertisement (rcv_wnd=0) for >15s. That's classic slow-consumer.
Maya: reproduction: `curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" https://api.eu.redwood.ai/v1/stream/ -o /dev/null` from a client with artificially throttled reader shows proxy buffer grows and then proxy write blocks. We should document this as client slow-consumer scenario.
Jay: longer term: propose server-side backpressure knobs: 1) limit max queued bytes per connection, 2) eject/soft-close connections if queue > X and client idle for >Y, 3) implement graceful polling fallback negotiation in SDKs.
Ryan: immediate next steps summary: - leave scaled replicas (8) - keep new timeouts for 2h - monitor p95/p99 - expand fallback canary to 50% if stable - create incident ticket and postmortem owner
Ana: creating incident ticket: INC-2026-341 (created). Linking case and runbook. 
Ana: perf numbers now: p95=820ms, p99=1.8s (post-mitigation) — still above SLO for p99 but trending down.
Maya: followup checks: ALB timeouts show increase in 504s a bit — need to watch. I adjusted ALB idle timeout from 60s -> 90s to avoid cutting long polling clients while we run changes.
Jay: deployed a hotfix to proxy to return `X-Stream-Status: queued` header when we hit per-connection queue threshold so clients can surface and optionally switch to polling.
Liz: support note: advising customers with problematic clients to upgrade SDK v2.1+ which can auto-fallback to polling on `X-Stream-Status: queued` and to prefer websocket mode for better flow control.
Bob: Acme confirmed they will try SDK update tomorrow. For now they're okay with polling fallback.
Ryan: handoff: I'm pausing active remediation, handing to Ana for overnight watch. Ana, you're now primary oncall. Call me if p99 > 3s or error rate > 0.5% or customer escalations.
Ana: taking over. I'll keep the scaled proxies and timeouts for now and check again in 30m. Creating a monitoring alert: `alert: streaming_slo_regression_eu` with cooldown 5m.
Maya: added traces link: https://dashboard.redwood.ai/traces/streaming?trace=1769995 - has traces of blocked write calls and backpressure spikes.
Ana: next-day action items (for postmortem): 1) implement per-tenant soft eject on slow-consumer 2) improve SDK fallback handshake 3) add test for proxy queue limit 4) update docs and runbook w/ reproduction steps and command snippets
Ryan: thanks team. tagging #incidents #eng-runtime #support. :thumbsup:
incidents-bot: Incident INC-2026-341 created and assigned to Ana. Severity: Sev2. Slack paging escalations sent to oncall rotation.
Liz: I'll follow up with customer tomorrow AM once postmortem actions are defined.
Bob: noted. closing customer loop after postmortem. thanks everyone.
